title: Groundnut Cultivation, Gypsum Application and Pegging Stage Advisory
source: ICAR - Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR), Junagadh
region: Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Rajasthan
content: Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) requires well-drained sandy loam or red sandy soils. Hard clay soils hinder peg penetration and pod harvesting. Seed rate: 100-110 kg kernels/ha for bunch types (e.g., TAG 24, JL 24, Kadiri 6); 90-100 kg/ha for spreading types. Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium culture (Bradyrhizobium) @ 10 g/kg seed and Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed. Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm for bunch varieties; 45 cm x 10 cm for semi-spreading varieties. Essential Gypsum Protocol: Apply Gypsum @ 400-500 kg/ha at flowering/pegging stage (40-45 DAS) close to the root zone and incorporate lightly. Why Gypsum is mandatory: Calcium is absorbed directly by the developing pods in the soil, not translocated from leaves. Calcium deficiency causes 'pops' (empty pods without kernels). Sulphur in gypsum boosts oil synthesis. Critical irrigation: Pegging stage (35-50 DAS) and pod development stage (55-75 DAS). Keep soil friable during pegging; do not disturb soil after peg penetration.
